page_title: How to Implement a Search Engine Part 3: Ranking tf-idf

summary.title: How to Implement a Search Engine Part 3: Ranking tf-idf
summary.one_liner: You learn how tf-idf term weighting, document normalization and cosine similarity turn unranked search matches into an ordered list of results.
takeaways: Term frequency counts term occurrences per document, normalized by document vector length to avoid favoring long documents.
Inverse document frequency is the log of N divided by document frequency, which downweights common terms like stopwords.
Tf-idf weight is the product of tf and idf, giving each document a sparse vector over the corpus vocabulary.
Queries and documents are normalized vectors, and cosine similarity (their dot product) ranks documents by angle to the query.
summary.summary: The article is the third part of a series on building a search engine in code. It explains how to rank query results using the tf-idf weighting scheme, starting from term frequency under a bag-of-words model and vector space representation. It then covers length normalization, inverse document frequency with a logarithm, and how the product forms sparse document vectors. Finally, it normalizes query and document vectors and ranks results by cosine similarity, with accompanying source code that returns the top 10 matches for a query.
